summary: This work develops a macroscopic description of 2D Pauli stabilizer codes and fault-tolerant logical operations using Majorana fermion motion, showing that braiding-based gates achieve lower space overhead than lattice surgery for near-term error rates. The framework captures code properties from lattice scales to asymptotic regimes, enabling compact design of fault-tolerant 2-qubit Clifford gates.
motivation: Efficient logical gate implementation on non-local encoded information requires optimizing space overhead and reducing physical qubit requirements for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors map planar Pauli codes to Majorana fermion configurations, define code distance via Wilson and 't Hooft line lengths on the Majorana graph, implement fault-tolerant motion through both isentropic and virtual particle protocols, and design braiding-based gates that densely pack Majorana fermions while maintaining distance. Numerical benchmarks using the SI1000 error model compare braiding protocols against lattice surgery on square-grid superconducting qubit devices.
result: Braiding-based 2-qubit Clifford gates require $4d^2 + O(d)$ physical qubits versus $6d^2 + O(d)$ for lattice surgery (asymptotic scaling advantage $\eta_{\mathrm{LS} \to B} \approx 0.184$), and simulations show higher fidelities even at small code distances for realistic error rates, with unoptimized circuits already satisfying the exponential advantage condition.
